1.why: Text uses a clean, legible sans-serif with decent line height (e.g., wrapped instructions on step 1), but letter spacing looks like default rather than noticeably generous.

2.why: All instructions are sentence case with no italics and no dense blocks; the only all-caps strings are the setup secret and recovery codes themselves, not instructions.

3.why: Every screen is a narrow single-column layout with full-width buttons and text that wraps cleanly at mobile width, e.g., steps 4 and 9.

4.why: Instructions are one to two short plain sentences throughout, e.g., 'Enter the six-digit code.' and 'Save them somewhere private.'

5.why: Every input shows an example: 'marcus@example.com' in the email field, 'Example: 123456' for identity and authenticator codes, and 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for recovery codes.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is two short sentences (e.g., steps 7 and 11), so no long block of text must be read to proceed.

7.why: A 'Copy setup secret' button accompanies the 32-character secret (step 6) and a 'Copy all codes' button accompanies the recovery codes (steps 8-9).

8.why: A 'Show QR setup pattern' button reveals a scannable QR code (step 5) as an alternative to the manual setup secret.

9.why: The fields are standard-looking inputs with a prefilled email, but no autofill or password-manager support (e.g., autocomplete cues) can actually be observed in the screenshots.

10.why: A four-segment progress bar shows position, headings are large and bold, and each screen has one prominent solid-blue primary button.

11.why: Each screen has a single dominant blue action, but the authenticator screen (steps 4-6) asks the user to add an account in the app, choose QR or manual secret, and enter a code before confirming.

12.why: Green banners state outcomes and next steps after each action, e.g., 'Identity checked. Next, set up your authenticator.' and 'New recovery codes created. Save them now.'

13.why: 'Request another code', show/hide toggles for the QR pattern, setup secret, and recovery codes, a 'Back' link, and re-testing of recovery codes are all offered with no visible penalty.

14.why: The one error shown, 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.' (step 14), states the problem and fix without blame, though 'page check' is slightly jargon-like and no wrong-code error was demonstrated.

15.why: No countdowns or reading timers appear on any step, but the 'Your page check expired' message (step 14) shows the page state does expire after idle time.
